name: Budapest
tagline: Two cities on either bank of the Danube: a hilltop castle in Buda, grand boulevards in Pest, thermal baths, ruin bars and a Parliament that glows at night.
highlight: The Parliament building lit up on the Danube at night, seen from a river cruise or the Buda bank.
shortDescription: Hungary's capital, with the Parliament, Buda Castle, Fisherman's Bastion, Széchenyi thermal baths, the Great Market Hall, ruin bars and Danube views.
metaDescription: A Budapest travel guide: Parliament, Buda Castle, Fisherman's Bastion, Chain Bridge, Széchenyi and Gellért baths, the Great Market Hall, ruin bars, food, where to stay and a four-day plan.
knownFor: Thermal baths, Danube views, ruin bars, architecture

image.alt: The Hungarian Parliament Building beside the Danube

intro: Budapest was created in 1873 from three towns, Buda, Óbuda and Pest, either side of the Danube, and it remains a city of two halves. Buda, on the west bank, is hilly and old, with the castle, the medieval Matthias Church and the Fisherman's Bastion on Castle Hill. Pest, on the east, is flat and busy, with wide boulevards, the neo-Gothic Parliament, cafés and the nightlife of the Jewish Quarter. Its riverbanks and Buda Castle Quarter are together a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Its golden age came in the late 19th century, when Budapest was the second capital of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, and much of its grandeur dates from then: the Opera House, St. Stephen's Basilica, the Chain Bridge and the Great Market Hall. Underneath, the city sits on more than 100 thermal springs, and bathing in hot pools, from the palatial Széchenyi to the Ottoman-era Rudas, is a central experience.

By night, Budapest turns lively. The ruin bars, set in abandoned buildings in the old Jewish Quarter, started the trend in the early 2000s, and Szimpla Kert is the best known. The food scene has grown too, with modern Hungarian restaurants alongside traditional goulash and chimney cake. Three or four days is ideal, and it is a good base for day trips.

attractionsIntro: Budapest's sights are on both sides of the river, linked by bridges and trams.

attractions.name: Parliament Building

image.file: File:Danube and Hungarian Parliament Building by night.jpg
image.alt: The illuminated Hungarian Parliament Building on the Danube at night

attractions.text: A neo-Gothic riverside palace opened in 1904, with 691 rooms, the Holy Crown of Hungary and a grand staircase, visited on guided tours.

attractions.name: Fisherman's Bastion and Matthias Church

image.alt: The white turrets of Fisherman's Bastion above the Danube

attractions.text: A fairy-tale terrace of white turrets with views across the Danube to Pest, beside the Gothic Matthias Church.
attractions.tip: Go at sunrise for no queue.

attractions.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath

image.alt: People bathing in the outdoor pools at Széchenyi Thermal Bath

attractions.text: A huge neo-baroque bath complex in City Park with outdoor pools, saunas and steam rooms, open year-round.

attractions.name: Great Market Hall

image.alt: The interior of Budapest's Great Market Hall with stalls under an iron roof

attractions.text: A grand 1897 market hall with stalls of paprika, salami and produce, and a food court upstairs serving lángos.

attractions.name: Chain Bridge

image.file: File:Széchenyi Chain Bridge in Budapest at night.jpg
image.alt: The Széchenyi Chain Bridge lit at night above the Danube

attractions.text: The first permanent bridge across the Danube in Budapest, opened in 1849, and lit at night.

attractions.name: St. Stephen's Basilica

image.alt: The dome of St. Stephen's Basilica above the city

attractions.text: The city's largest church, with a dome you can climb for 360-degree views.

attractions.name: Szimpla Kert

image.alt: The eclectic courtyard of Szimpla Kert ruin bar

attractions.text: The original ruin bar, in a former stove factory, with mismatched furniture and lively courtyards.

thingsToDoIntro: Budapest is for baths, boats and bars.

thingsToDo.text: A scenic line beside the Danube.

foodIntro: Budapest's food ranges from cheap market stalls to fine dining.

gettingThere.intro: Budapest has an international airport and rail links.

options.text: Bus 100E to the centre, about 40 minutes.

bestTime.headline: April–June and September–October
bestTime.summary: Budapest has hot summers and cold winters.

seasons.text: Cold, with Christmas markets and steaming baths.
